raw_response:
I've been farming these 19 mu for 30 years, and at 58 I know every piece of it. My son works in Shijiazhuang now, so it's mostly me and my wife handling things, with three mouths to feed total. I finished middle school, so I can read the extension leaflets, but honestly I trust what I've seen with my own eyes more than what some young technician writes on paper.

It's late April now, so the wheat I planted last October is at jointing stage. The extension station says 15 kg nitrogen per mu is enough, but I've learned that 17 kg is safer on my land — the soil here is a bit sandy and leaches. I'll topdress about 10 kg of urea per mu this week while the wheat is jointing. I already put down compound fertilizer as base last fall. I'll irrigate three times total: now at jointing, once at booting in May, and once at grain filling if it stays dry. The well water costs money, so I watch it, but I won't skip irrigation — a bad wheat year hurts more than saving a few hundred yuan on pumping.

For cotton, I've got about 9 mu ready. I'll plow this week and plant by April 25 — same variety as last year, I know it. Cotton needs less fertilizer than grain, around 12 kg nitrogen per mu total, split between base and flowering stage. The real headache is insects, especially bollworm. I'll spray insecticide 3–4 times and weed once with herbicide. Cotton picking is labor-intensive — my wife and I will do most of it, but I'll hire 5 days of help for the peak picks in September.

Maize comes after wheat harvest in early June. There's no time for fancy tillage — wheat comes off, I rotary till the same day, and maize goes in immediately with hybrid seed. I'll put compound fertilizer in the planting hole and maybe side-dress urea at big trumpet stage if the plants look hungry. Maize usually gives me 480 kg/mu if the summer rains cooperate. I'll irrigate twice: at silking and grain filling.

I'm cash-conscious this year. Fertilizer prices are up again. I've budgeted about 15,600 yuan for all inputs. I won't experiment — I need reliable yields, not surprises. Wheat-maize is my bread and butter; cotton gives me cash income in the fall. If I get 450 kg/mu on wheat and 480 kg/mu on maize, plus 250 kg/mu seed cotton, we'll be okay.
